statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-53613: for a restricted (non-root) mount request authorised by an /etc/fstab entry with the user or users option, libmount checks the mount target and then lets the mount system call resolve the target path again, so a local user who can write to an ancestor directory of that target can swap a path component with renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) and have the mount land on a root-owned location such as /etc/sudoers.d, gaining root. https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-8gj5-72r3-428g lists 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 as patched. On the 2.41 branch the fix is https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/0b010025a0e429bc80355c94db86a843395d49e2 with https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/a9508d216eb8977979102782672e0470cc9bf2a2, both in the v2.41.5 tag and not in v2.41.4: libmount pins the target with an O_PATH file descriptor opened without following symlinks, mounts onto that descriptor with the new mount API and verifies the mount ID afterwards. Caveat: when libmount falls back to the legacy mount(2) system call (for example on a kernel without the new mount API) the target is still resolved by path; the CVE record therefore lists 2.41 releases through 2.41.6 as affected, upstream documents the limitation in mount(8), and only 2.42.4 also pins legacy targets (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53613). Alpine lists the CVE under 2.41.6-r0 in the 3.23-stable main/util-linux APKBUILD secfixes; no 2.41.5 build was published for Alpine 3.23. Checked libmount in every published build of this owner for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64: 2.41.2-r0 and 2.41.4-r0 lack the target-pinning code, and 2.41.6-r0 and 2.41.6-r1 contain it (its 'failed to pin target', 'reopen target fd' and 'target mount ID verified' debug messages). The range ends at 2.41.6-r0, the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-53613: for a restricted (non-root) mount request authorised by an /etc/fstab entry with the user or users option, libmount checks the mount target and then lets the mount system call resolve the target path again, so a local user who can write to an ancestor directory of that target can swap a path component with renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) and have the mount land on a root-owned location such as /etc/sudoers.d, gaining root. https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-8gj5-72r3-428g lists 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 as patched. On the 2.41 branch the fix is https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/0b010025a0e429bc80355c94db86a843395d49e2 with https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/a9508d216eb8977979102782672e0470cc9bf2a2, both in the v2.41.5 tag and not in v2.41.4: libmount pins the target with an O_PATH file descriptor opened without following symlinks, mounts onto that descriptor with the new mount API and verifies the mount ID afterwards. Caveat: when libmount falls back to the legacy mount(2) system call (for example on a kernel without the new mount API) the target is still resolved by path; the CVE record therefore lists 2.41 releases through 2.41.6 as affected, upstream documents the limitation in mount(8), and only 2.42.4 also pins legacy targets (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53613). Debian fixed it for trixie in util-linux 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6442-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-53613), a new upstream 2.41.5 release whose changelog names this CVE. The DHI util-linux packages built from that Debian source carry it: the shipped changelog of every published build from that source records it, and the published libmount1 on amd64 and arm64 contains the target-pinning code. The range ends at the lowest such build still published. Builds made from Debian's earlier 2.41-5 source sort below it and are reported as affected, including later ones that carried a DHI backport of the fix.
